label: D2 after choosing a2, scaled by D2 policy leaning back to a1 and by a switch from a1
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * last_is("a2 S1 r") ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * np.maximum(choice, 0)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only after the agent chose a2 (seen as in_action at D2); it is silent at D1 and GO and after a1 choices. Magnitude is graded by the model policy logit at D2: the more the D2 policy leans toward a1 (choice > 0, i.e. weak or reversing a2 preference), the larger it is (largest weight). It is also raised when the a2 choice is a switch from a1 on the previous trial (+~0.65), and after a previous a2 S1 rewarded trial (rare-rewarded, model-based says switch, yet a2 repeated). The previous-unrewarded term adds little. The reached state and the hidden good state add nothing. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.63 (dev 0.64), above the profile all ceiling 0.53 because the graded policy term is used. Observed-history-only version (a2 at D2 x previous switch / previous reward / a2 S1 r / a2 S1 u / choice two trials back) gets test 0.43. No future variables used.

issues: The policy term is described with the wrong shape. The label says activation grows as the D2 policy leans back to a1 (choice > 0). In fact it rises linearly from about choice = -2, while the policy still favours a2. Replacing np.maximum(choice,0) with np.maximum(choice+2,0) raises test R^2 from 0.622 to 0.695 (3 terms, against the claimed 4-term 0.626). With both ramps in one fit, np.maximum(choice,0) gets weight -0.01 and np.maximum(choice+1.5,0) gets 0.39. The profile shows the same thing: the D2 residual by policy decile peaks at decile 5 and is negative at deciles 7-8 (-0.064, -0.087), so it is not 'larger the more it leans to a1'.

'Switch from a1' lumps together previous-trial patterns with unequal effects. Fitted per pattern (test 0.638): a1 S1 u 0.85, a1 S1 r 0.94, a1 S2 r 0.44, a1 S2 u 0.26. Misses on the claimed terms show the largest systematic over-prediction at D2 after a1 S2 r (-0.123): a rare-rewarded a1 trial (where model-based logic says switch to a2) gives a smaller boost than the single prev_action==1 weight assumes.
The prev_reward==0 term is dead weight (0.04). Dropping it leaves test R^2 at 0.622 (vs 0.626), so it should not be listed as a component.
The observed-only claim is slightly understated: per-pattern previous-trial terms times (D2 & a2) reach test 0.449, not 0.43. This is minor.

Confirmed claims: the feature is silent at D1 and GO; it is negative or near zero after a1 at D2 (adding a D2&a1 term changes little); the hidden good state adds nothing; a2 S1 r carries a +0.25 boost; no future variables are used. a2 alone at D2 explains only 0.04, so the graded policy term carries most of the fit (0.44 on its own).
skeptic.revised_label: D2 after choosing a2: grows linearly as the a2 preference weakens (policy logit above about -2, not only once it favours a1). It is boosted after a switch from an a1 trial, most after a1 S1 r/u and least after a1 S2 r/u, and modestly after a2 S1 r.
skeptic.better_terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * last_is('a1 S1 u') ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * last_is('a1 S2 r') ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * last_is('a1 S1 r') ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * last_is('a1 S2 u') ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * last_is('a2 S1 r') ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * np.maximum(choice+1.5, 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * np.maximum(choice, 0)

final_label: D2 after choosing a2: grows linearly as the a2 preference weakens (policy logit above about -2, not only once it favours a1). It is boosted after a switch from an a1 trial, most after a1 S1 r/u and least after a1 S2 r/u, and modestly after a2 S1 r.
